Sign flips: invaded high is 52.51 t C/ha against pristine 55.78 (down) and against degraded 32.21 (up). states_counterfactual coded 0 conservatively under rule 2 because no verbatim counterfactual construction was seen, though the paper does reason about alternative management futures
30 plots per condition of 2500 m2. No land-use history of the uninvaded comparison reported. Authors state the study is a one-time survey and call for long-term monitoring

Stand ages reported per fragment, 4-12 yr invaded and 5-20 yr non-invaded, and modelled explicitly. Note the reference is itself young second growth rather than mature forest, which is an unstated counterfactual choice: comparing to regrowth rather than to the mature system the site would eventually reach

system: Phragmites australis / Long Island Sound USA
note: Two marshes, three seasons. Authors conclude no consistent evidence that invasion significantly impacts carbon stocks. Core depth varies 2.2 to 29.0 cm against a stated 20-30 cm, confounding the reported seasonal effect with sampling depth

Six paired sites against three different native vegetation types (sawgrass marsh, pine flatwoods, cypress dome), which are pooled as one reference. Soil total carbon reported as a percentage with no bulk density, so no areal stock is recoverable

Carries a restored class with an explicit recovery timeline, biomass carbon reaching 71-73 per cent of intact stands roughly 20 years after planting. One of very few post-removal or post-restoration carbon trajectories in the whole literature
